change: Submitted custom native-form text activates existing persistent chat-only quarantine. Per-form trust values prevent ordinary approval-like text from allowing. Desktop descriptions include the warning. Classifier and Agent Monitor implementations unchanged.

packaged_live_tests.installation: Standalone immutable release-layout packages without node_modules; actual pinned OpenCode 2.0.22; no external LLM

native_forms.custom_answers: Actual form.reply accepts Russian free text at pre and literal allow at post. Both activate quarantine; continuation and next user turn have no tools or additional approvals; two native execution.succeeded events and no interrupted/failed events per custom case.

packaged_live_tests.interaction: Native session/form APIs and local deterministic model; visual UI clicks not automated

review.status: focused independent source review of native approval change; no consequential defects reported
verified: Only the bound per-form random trust option value returns allow; all other structurally valid string replies return quarantine, including literal allow and displayed labels.
Form identity, immutable checkpoint binding, cancellation and cleanup checks are retained. Previous-form trust values cannot approve a later checkpoint.
The Desktop-rendered description includes warning, tool and bounded reason. custom=true allows the server to deliver arbitrary typed text to the plugin.
Existing classifier, Agent Monitor integration and quarantine enforcement are unchanged.

limits: OpenCode forms expose no input-origin metadata. Manually submitting the exact random trust value for the current form is indistinguishable from selecting its option. Ordinary typed text selects quarantine; Desktop blank input remains pending.
The default classifier is still an always-deny stub; classifier unavailability fails open only outside an active quarantine.
The native choices and custom-text quarantine apply to backend=stub. Agent Monitor uses its own strict policy and trusted operator approval; native forms cannot override it.
Already-running tools can finish; post quarantine cannot undo side effects. This plugin is not an OS sandbox.
Tool removal is applied at context/generate/compaction hooks. Other plugins and actions outside local hooks are outside this enforcement guarantee; run the sensor last.
A failed quarantine write keeps the current instance blocked but cannot guarantee persistence after restart.
New independent sessions are not quarantined; descendants inherit by parentID, not by fork provenance.
Explicitly disabling the sensor or changing its state directory changes enforcement; local state is not protected from a user or external process with filesystem access.
No dedicated assistant message is inserted; exact subsequent LLM wording is not guaranteed.
Native API integration tested; no manual Desktop/TUI visual click test.
Noninteractive opencode run cancels native forms; use Desktop or interactive TUI for manual approval.
Self-load failures before hook registration cannot be enforced by the plugin.

previous_release_validation.note: Historical checks, not rerun against 0.4.1. Current focused native cases cover the changed approval path. Agent Monitor and quarantine runtime are unchanged; current unit/component tests also cover them.
